% Energy table (Table 3) -- generated from real measured data only
\begin{table}[width=.9\linewidth,cols=6,pos=htbp]
\caption{Theoretical Energy per Graph (analytic SOP model, 1-shot, MUTAG/PROTEINS/ENZYMES)}
\label{tab:energy}
\centering \scriptsize
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3pt}
\begin{tabular}{@{} >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.26\linewidth} c c c c c @{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Method} & \textbf{MUTAG} & \textbf{PROTEINS} & \textbf{ENZYMES} & \textbf{Mean} & \textbf{Red.}\% \\
\midrule
Proto-GCN & 4.09 & 8.99 & 7.50 & 6.86 & 49.6\% \\
Proto-GIN & 8.14 & 17.83 & 14.87 & 13.61 & 0.0\% \\
Proto-SAGE & 8.14 & 17.83 & 14.87 & 13.61 & 0.0\% \\
MSG* & 4.50 & 9.89 & 8.25 & 7.55 & 44.6\% \\
Spike-GNN (Euc.) ($\bar{r}$=0.40) & 5.27 & 10.95 & 9.17 & 8.46 & 37.8\% \\
SpikeRPGNN ($\bar{r}$=0.41) & 5.69 & 11.40 & 9.55 & 8.88 & 34.8\% \\
\bottomrule
\multicolumn{6}{p{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\tabcolsep\relax}}{\scriptsize Energy $E=\mathrm{SOP}\times e$ with $e_{FLOP}=4.6$ pJ (dense) and $e_{SOP}=0.9$ pJ \citep{Horowitz14}. A spiking model emits $\bar{r}\times\mathrm{FLOPs}$ synaptic events on each of its $T=8$ integration steps, so its count is $\mathrm{SOP}_{spiking}=T\times\bar{r}\times\mathrm{FLOPs}_{dense}$ with the measured firing rate $\bar{r}$; a dense baseline performs a single forward pass and carries no $T$ factor. Including $T$ is required for the comparison to be like-for-like, and it reduces the advantage over the dense reference from a naive $1-\bar{r}\,e_{SOP}/e_{FLOP}$ to the values reported here. FLOPs are analytic per-architecture counts. Reductions are relative to the capacity- and backbone-matched dense Proto-GIN. MSG* is charged at the dense $e_{FLOP}$ rate because its legacy baseline implementation did not record firing rates; under the $T$-aware model an $e_{SOP}$ charge would lower its energy only while $T\bar{r}<e_{FLOP}/e_{SOP}$, i.e.\ while $\bar{r}<0.64$ at $T=8$, and since that rate was never recorded we charge the dense rate and flag the sign of the correction as untested; its hidden dimension is set to the same width ($128$) as every other method, so that neither accuracy nor energy is confounded by model capacity. The spike-driven event counts were independently re-derived by traversing the emitted spike events over their incident edges (a production-path hook, a PyTorch reference, and a pure-NumPy reference), and all three agree exactly; the $e_{SOP}$/$e_{FLOP}$ per-operation constants remain literature values, not device measurements.}
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\multicolumn{8}{p{\dimexpr\tblwidth-6\tabcolsep\relax}}{\scriptsize $^{*}p<0.05$, $^{**}p<0.01$, $^{***}p<0.001$; ns: not significant at $q<0.05$. $d$ is Cohen's $d_{z}$ (mean difference over the SD of those differences) on the paired cells and standard Cohen's $d$ (df-weighted pooled SD) on the 12 Welch cells. The capacity-matched grid comprises $60$ cells (six baselines $\times$ five datasets $\times$ two shots) and all 60 of them are corrected in one BH-FDR family. On DD and Rdt-M5k at 1-shot SpikeRPGNN has $10$ runs against a baseline's $5$, so those 12 cells use Welch's test. They are retained rather than dropped: excluding them would shrink the correction family and make every surviving $q$-value smaller, which is the direction that flatters the proposed method. Both accuracies of every cell are reported in Table~\ref{tab:main_results}.}
\end{tabular*}

% Ablation table (ENZYMES, real data, 50ep re-run)
\begin{table}[width=.9\linewidth,cols=5,pos=htbp]
\caption{Ablation Study on ENZYMES (5-way 1-shot, 5 runs per variant, paired $t$-tests vs.\ Full)}
\label{tab:ablation}
\centering \scriptsize
\begin{tabular}{@{} l c c c c @{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Config.} & \textbf{Acc.\ (\%)} & \textbf{$E$ ($\mu$J/g)$^\dagger$} & \textbf{$\Delta$Acc} & \textbf{$p$-val} \\
\midrule
Full SpikeRPGNN & 23.6$\pm$1.5 & --- & --- & --- \\
w/o Spikes & 22.8$\pm$2.0 & 14.87 & -0.8\% & 0.365 \\
w/o STMP & 24.2$\pm$1.0 & --- & +0.6\% & 0.281 \\
w/o Riem.\ (Euc.) & 23.1$\pm$1.6 & --- & -0.6\% & 0.134 \\
w/o Fr\'echet & 23.6$\pm$1.5 & --- & +0.0\% & --- \\
w/o DvM & 23.2$\pm$0.8 & --- & -0.4\% & 0.511 \\
w/o Meta & 22.1$\pm$1.5 & --- & -1.6\% & 0.033 \\
\bottomrule
\multicolumn{5}{p{\dimexpr\linewidth-2\tabcolsep\relax}}{\scriptsize $^\dagger$ Analytic SOP model (\S\ref{sec:energy}); $E$ is reported only where the firing rate was reliably measured: Full uses the measured $\bar{r}$ of the main ENZYMES 1-shot runs (the value reported in Table~\ref{tab:energy}), and w/o Spikes is charged at the dense GIN FLOP cost. Firing rates of the remaining spiking variants were not isolated from the support-set spike accumulation, so they are not assigned energy values. w/o STMP removes the spiking temporal message-passing loop altogether (a single non-spiking RGC pass plus pooling), so it emits no spikes and is not on the same event-driven accounting; it is therefore also left unvalued. All seven variants in this table share the unified 50-epoch episodic protocol of Section~\ref{sec:setup} with 5 runs per configuration, and the Full row is the ablation's own 50-epoch, 5-run SpikeRPGNN, so every $\Delta$ and $p$-value is computed within a single controlled study (the 1-shot no-op of w/o Fr\'echet requires this internal comparison). The Full mean is statistically indistinguishable from the main-results-table SpikeRPGNN (Table~\ref{tab:main_results}); the ${\sim}1$ percentage-point gap is run-to-run variance at a matched protocol, not a protocol change. w/o Fr\'echet is identical to Full in the 1-shot setting: the Fr\'echet mean of a single support point is the point itself.}
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
